issues.failure_explanation: The standing assumptions give only $f\in C^1$ and $V\in C^2$, while the proof uses a uniform order-$p$ local-error bound $O(h^{p+1})$ for the surrogate field $f-\alpha\nabla V$. For general $p>1$, that estimate is not supplied by the stated regularity. The theorem itself does not add the $C^p/C^{p+1}$ assumptions appearing in the earlier quoted theorem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add sufficient smoothness and uniform local-error hypotheses for the chosen order-$p$ method, and consistently choose the compact neighborhood in which the numerical step and exact flow remain.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed proof does not establish positive invariance for the full stated class of one-step methods and standing regularity assumptions.
issues.title: Uniform local-truncation estimate lacks the required regularity hypotheses
issues.why_classification: This is a standard local hypothesis repair that preserves the invariant-set conclusion, method, and rate without changing the proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
U^{\varepsilon}_{h,\alpha} \coloneqq 
\bigl\{\,x + t\,h\,Y_h(x)\ \big|\ x\in U^{\varepsilon},\ t\in[0,1]\,\bigr\},
\quad\text{where } Y_h(x):= f(x)-\alpha\,\nabla V(x).

where $(R, \Omega) \in \mathrm{SO}(3) \times \mathbb{R}^3$ in standard settings, and $\mathbb{I}$ is the moment of inertia matrix. To apply feedback integrator, we assume that the system is defined through the same expressions in~\eqref{eq:dynamics_rigid} in $\mathbb{R}^{3\times 3} \times \mathbb{R}^3$.

issues.failure_explanation: By definition, membership in $U^\varepsilon$ requires membership in $M$. Euler line segments in the ambient embedding generally leave a curved manifold. For example, in the rigid-body example the segment starting at $R=I$ in direction $R\widehat\Omega$ has matrices $I+t h\widehat\Omega$, which are generally not orthogonal for $t h\ne0$. Hence $U^\varepsilon_{h,\beta/h}\subseteq U^\varepsilon$ is false as defined, independently of how small $h$ is. The proof instead reasons with ambient sublevel sets of $V$.

failure_location.quote: For any $\varepsilon \in (0, \nu)$ and $\beta \in \left(0, \frac{2}{L}\right)$, there exists $h_0 > 0$ such that for each $0 < h < h_0$, $U^\varepsilon_{h, \frac{\beta}{h}} \subseteq U^\varepsilon$ and thus $V^{-1}([0, \varepsilon])$ is positive invariant under respective discrete systems~\eqref{eq:feedback_discrete_system} defined with $\alpha = \frac{\beta}{h}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine $U^\varepsilon$ as the ambient sublevel set $V^{-1}([0,\varepsilon])$ inside the extension domain, revise all associated suprema accordingly, and explicitly prove that the entire Euler segment—not merely its endpoint—remains in that ambient sublevel set. The adaptive proofs must then be checked with the corrected ambient sets.
issues.overall_effect: The fixed-gain theorem's principal inclusion is false, and the adaptive-gain results inherit the incompatible domain and bounds through their repeated use of $U^\varepsilon$ and the proof of this theorem.
issues.title: The set used in the fixed-gain theorem is restricted to the manifold and cannot contain Euler segments
issues.why_classification: Although the intended ambient-set repair is apparent, the incompatible definition is used throughout the fixed and adaptive arguments and requires coordinated revisions and an explicit segment-invariance argument, rather than a single routine local edit.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: U_{h,x_k, \beta} \coloneqq \bigl\{ x_k + u f(x_k) - v \nabla V(x_k) \mid u\in[0,h], v \in \left[0, \beta\right] \bigr\}.

issues.failure_explanation: The left side includes the nontrivial tube $U_{h,x_{k_0},\beta_{k_0}}$, but the sum begins at $\ell=1$. In particular, when $\tau=1$ the estimate claims that the Hessian norm everywhere on this tube is at most its value $H_{x_{k_0}}$ at the base point, which does not follow from Lipschitz continuity and is generally false. A Lipschitz increment for the initial tube is missing.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Include the omitted $\ell=0$ displacement in the Lipschitz estimate and propagate the resulting factor—typically replacing $\tau-1$ by $\tau$ and $n-1$ by $n$—through the blockwise tube conditions.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed inclusion of all tubes in a gain-update block into $K_{x_{k_0}}$ is not established, so the frozen-gain descent estimate used to prove positive invariance is unsupported.
issues.title: Blockwise Hessian-tube estimate omits the first local displacement
issues.why_classification: The correction is local and routine, and the later bounds already allow an additive one-step term; it need not alter the theorem's qualitative guarantee.
